question: Q#119 (outline 9.4.8.1.1): e56a68e651c2 runs a verdict's instruments three at a time. Each sealed run gets its own ~/.cairn, but the repo, /tmp, the network and git are shared by all three (measured 2026-11-16), so a red can come from a neighbour rather than from the proof. (a) CC's recommendation: re-run a red once, alone, before recording it, and keep both readings on the verdict; a red that turns green alone is recorded as a contention red. (b) Record the red as it came: no extra time, and a contention red falls to the builder to read. Which should the verdict do, (a) or (b)?
why_it_blocks: e56a's falsifier and build differ by the answer: (a) adds a serial re-run clause and a second reading on the verdict; (b) adds nothing. BUILDME waits on it.

notes.text: Same question as open-27d456e96db3, which the outline check raised for Q#119. One answer answers both.
